steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: A hierarchical structure has many layers of management: clear chain of command but slow decision-making and communication can be distorted through layers. | Key Fact: A flat structure has few management layers: faster communication and decision-making, more responsibility for employees, but managers have wider spans of control (more direct reports). | Key Fact: Span of control is the number of subordinates a manager directly supervises: narrow span = closer supervision but more management layers; wide span = less supervision, fewer layers. | Key Fact: Chain of command is the line of authority from top to bottom: in a hierarchy, instructions flow down and reports flow up. Delayering removes middle management layers to speed up communication.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain two advantages and two disadvantages of a flat organisational structure. | Describe the difference between centralisation and decentralisation, and give one benefit of each. | Evaluate whether a large business should delayer its hierarchical structure.
